Random walk with drift on log death rates

Source: R/model-rwd.R
rwd.Rd

Benchmark model: the log death rate of every age follows a random walk with drift, y[t] = y[t-1] + mu + e[t]. The drift is estimated from the last drift_window years. Draws include drift uncertainty and innovations:

Usage

rwd(
  drift_window = NULL,
  innovations = c("bootstrap", "gaussian"),
  observation_noise = FALSE
)

Arguments

drift_window

Number of most recent years used for drift and innovations (NULL: all years).

innovations

"bootstrap" or "gaussian".

observation_noise

Deprecated: model the log rates as a random walk plus noise (see Details); use arima_series(order = c(0, 1, 1), drift = TRUE).

Value

A model specification.

Details

  • "bootstrap" (default): innovations are age vectors resampled from the observed year-to-year changes, which keeps the correlation between ages; the drift of each path is the mean of a bootstrap sample of those changes;

  • "gaussian": independent normal innovations per age with the estimated variance, and normal drift uncertainty.

Zero death counts are replaced by 0.5 before taking logs. The draws describe observed rates, so predictive draws add nothing.

Deprecated: observation_noise = TRUE. This variant treats the log rate as a random walk with drift observed with noise (a local level model with drift), with variances estimated by a moment estimator of this package without a published source: from the variance and first autocovariance of the year-to-year changes, the noise variance as the Poisson part (one over the deaths) plus an extra part common to all ages, clamped to at most 0.45 times the variance of the changes, the level variance to at least 0.1 times it, and shrunk towards the median of the ages with a prior standard deviation of three times that median; the level is Kalman filtered and the draws are paths of the level, to which predictive draws add Poisson variation of the deaths. It still works and warns (class mt_warning_deprecated). The published equivalent is the local level model with drift fitted by maximum likelihood (Harvey 1989), whose reduced form for the observed log rates is ARIMA(0,1,1) with drift: arima_series(order = c(0, 1, 1), drift = TRUE). With a drift_window, the variant is fitted to the years of the window and fitted rates of earlier years are missing.

References

Harvey AC (1989). Forecasting, Structural Time Series Models and the Kalman Filter. Cambridge University Press.

See also

arima_series().

Examples

x <- mt_example(deaths = "single")
fc <- mt_forecast(mt_fit(rwd(drift_window = 15), x), h = 5, n_draws = 100, seed = 1)
